configuration_schema.description: A closed structural JSON Schema 2020-12 subset: every reachable arbitrary object value explicitly closes its fields and every array declares closed item schemas. Local acyclic JSON Pointer references resolve only to schema positions; remote or dynamic references, nested identities and unresolved targets reject. Conjunctions may refine an already closed boundary. const, enum, default and examples contain literal data, never nested schemas.

component_schema.description: Uses the same closed structural subset as configuration_schema, including schema-aware literal handling and local acyclic references.

implemented.description: Exact implemented role methods. Every mutating method requires the same role reconciliation method; role membership alone does not establish that capability. Mutation admission also requires current observe authority for the same accepted instance and scope so uncertain effects can be inspected without replacing the executor identity. Later permission revocation remains effective and may block recovery.

source_schema.description: Uses the same closed structural subset as configuration_schema. Source-owned data cannot supply unconstrained nested objects or arrays to an accepted implementation.

MutationNamespace.description: One receiving-owner-verified canonical native mutation domain and facet. The receiving owner must resolve aliases and verify that distinct namespaces are actually disjoint, including native effects reached through host concerns and other owners. Different strings, adapter roles, or logical scopes do not establish separation. A resource may have separate lifecycle and resource-envelope facets when their native effects are disjoint.

authority.description: Canonical identity of the native administrative boundary, shared by all controllers that address it. This is not a fresh identity chosen by each adapter or scope owner.

MutationAuthority.description: Owner-accepted enrollment data, never a request authority token. A controller equal to the enrolled instance owns this scoped mutation boundary; another controller must already own the same scope and cover every listed native namespace. Delegates execute only through that controller's owning boundary and inherit its accepted binding, admission, holds, durable attempt and resource policies. Independent controllers may not overlap. Native interpretation must confine every request target and side effect to these verified domains; local record comparisons are not native qualification.

RuntimeBinding.description: An owner-accepted runtime identity. Its stable binding digest is digest(canonical JSON of this record with only admission_generation omitted); every other field participates. Host app assignment, App runtime selection and this instance must agree at new admission. Source drift requires an explicit owner rebind and never retargets accepted work. Admission generation is a mutable cessation fence and is not deployment identity. Active bindings require instance_digest. A binding without that pin is retained under inhibition solely to preserve accepted work and uncertainty: it remains readable, cancellable before dispatch and settleable after dispatch, but cannot admit new work, open admission or authorize dispatch. The owner must never infer or backfill its missing authority from current enrollment.

instance_digest.description: Digest of the exact accepted runtime Instance, including configuration, generation and mutation grants. Required at bind, preparation, admission opening and dispatch; the current scope must also retain change access and name this instance as its own mutation controller. The field is structurally optional only so inhibited bindings retain custody of accepted work without inventing authority.

binding_digest.description: The stable RuntimeBinding digest, computed over its canonical JSON with only admission_generation omitted. The receiving runtime owner must match it to the accepted binding before preparing a new effect.

ObservationBarrier.description: A fresh observation challenge issued by the controlling owner only after admission is closed and every previously accepted effect in the scope has settled. owner and scope identify the exact authority epoch; binding_digest pins the complete accepted runtime binding, including its approved executor configuration and grants, independently of the separately named admission_generation. exclusion_id identifies one continuously held, independently verified native exclusion of every writer capable of changing that scope. Releasing and reacquiring exclusion changes that identity. These fields are correlation data, never bearer authority or a caller assertion that exclusion is held. The adapter begins its complete scan after receiving this challenge and echoes it unchanged. Native exclusion remains held through proof consumption and the protected action. New accepted work, dispatch, settlement, binding or admission changes invalidate outstanding challenges and cached clearance for the affected scope. A challenge is consumed at most once; process restart and restored state require a fresh challenge. Wall-clock timestamps or an admission generation alone do not establish this causal ordering.

health.description: The observed result of a supported health check; unknown does not imply failure.

health_check.description: Whether this adapter can perform the relevant health check. Unsupported or unknown capability cannot establish healthy or unhealthy.

barrier.description: The exact request challenge echoed after the complete native scan. Null identifies an ordinary observation, which cannot establish protected quiescence. The receiving owner must independently verify the still-current challenge, approved binding, permission and continuously held native exclusion before consuming this evidence.

RuntimeControl.description: Durable owner-authored control for one delegated service apply attempt. The exact source target and complete enablement/activity/event intent remain with the attempt. Running or oneshot intent requires open admission; stopped intent requires closed admission. The target must equal an independently enrolled lifecycle namespace under the accepted runtime controller. No caller-supplied control creates dispatch authority.

runtime_control.description: Present only for a service lifecycle effect delegated to a runtime owner. Its absence never grants a service executor runtime dispatch authority; direct runtime and other independently owned effects retain their original attempt representation.

EffectAttempt.description: Owner-retained identity and state of one authorized native mutation. executor pins the complete receiving-owner-approved instance, configuration and grants; it is never resolved through a replacement enrollment. input_digest covers the exact canonical role request, excluding this attempt and its invocation wrapper. Those request bytes and every immutable referenced input remain in owner custody. Mutable state, outcome and native task knowledge do not change the attempt identity. Native dispatch requires an Invocation released by the controlling owner after durable acceptance; this record alone grants no execution authority.

EffectResult.description: The observed result of the exact invocation attempt. Known effects include a verified no-op that already satisfies the requested postcondition; success still requires the original method result identities and custody. A native process ending without required outputs does not establish a satisfied terminal result. Unknown outcomes retain uncertainty and are reconciled observationally.

Qualification.description: Native qualification requires passing linear-growth and complete-extent cases in addition to the independently selected behavioral cases. The receiving owner supplies the exact implemented method set from its approved descriptor. Every mutator also requires a passing reconcile-<role>-<method> case covering lost acknowledgment, independently reconstructed original input, and recovery of complete method-specific output without redispatch. A generic smoke or reconciliation case cannot qualify another method. Complete extent includes all pages and chunks; a total-list bound requires explicit maintainer approval before accepting or merging the implementation.

Snapshot.description: Exact captured dataset and complete immutable artifact closure, bound to the capture adapter Instance that produced it. The producer role is capture. A destination or procedure digest cannot substitute for this input identity. Cross-owner restore may use a different target binding only through independently authorized custody and destination mapping.

Counter.description: One observed usage quantity for an opaque approved allocation, never a limit or spare-capacity grant. Memory, swap, task, storage and inode values are instantaneous at observed_at. CPU time and I/O bytes are accumulated over [interval_start, observed_at]; complete evidence requires a nonempty positive interval and a value. I/O target is an approved logical device/domain handle, not a native path. Incomplete coverage cannot prove a hard bound; unsupported or unknown evidence cannot carry a numeric value. Counters in one response are unique by allocation, metric and target.

hard_isolation.description: True only when effective byte and inode capacities are enforced for the entire allocation domain; false is observational/advisory and cannot satisfy a hard allocation request.

capacity_bytes.description: Native observed effective enforced allocation ceiling in bytes, distinct from backing-store provisioning. Successful allocation requires equality with the exact reviewed ceiling; unsupported granularity or rounding requires renewed review. Zero means a hard zero-sized allocation, never unlimited.

capacity_inodes.description: Native observed effective enforced allocation ceiling in inodes, distinct from backing-store provisioning. Successful allocation requires equality with the exact reviewed ceiling; unsupported granularity or rounding requires renewed review. Zero means no inodes, never unlimited.

expires_at.description: The authoritatively observed effective expiration time, or null only when unknown/not applicable. Null cannot satisfy a bounded issuance or renewal.

valid_from.description: Authoritatively observed start/renewal instant of this effective lease validity. Null is permitted only when temporal validity is not known; it cannot satisfy a new issue/renew result.

CredentialLease.description: One exact credential lease and its observed validity, bound to its issuer Instance and consumer. Lease and value handles are opaque protected references, not plaintext or bearer authority. Multiple leases may overlap for one identity/consumer; rotating or revoking one does not authorize changes to another.

InstanceReference.description: Exact receiving-owner-approved adapter Instance and scope. installation_digest identifies its immutable artifact; configuration_digest and instance_digest bind the accepted configuration and complete enrollment including grants. New admission must match all fields against the independently loaded approved Instance. This record is identity data, never enrollment, dispatch authority or proof of native capability. Historical input producers may differ from the current executor; consuming their artifacts requires separately verified custody and an explicit accepted mapping.

SecretPublicationPredecessor.description: Exact prior published artifact in one secret-source instance and entry. Publication intent must match this source and entry and select a different immutable version before admission or dispatch. The receiver independently compares this predecessor with current provider state before changing its target; a mismatch requires renewed review. Null predecessor requires verified absence, never disables comparison. artifact_digest identifies the protected publication artifact, not a hash of a low-entropy plaintext secret.

LeaseReference.description: Exact issuer-scoped immutable lease identity. The issuer role is credential-issuer. Lease handles must not be rebound to replacement credentials. Renewal and revocation apply only to this lease and cannot select the latest lease, all leases for an identity or another consumer. A stale issuer binding requires explicit review, never implicit reinterpretation.

Invocation.description: The executable owner-to-adapter boundary for one mutation: its exact retained attempt and original typed role request. The role request by itself is planning data and cannot be dispatched. attempt.input_digest is the digest of request alone, avoiding a circular identity; executor belongs to the immutable attempt identity. The controlling owner must verify retained input/artifact custody, current permission, admission and native exclusion before release. An adapter must not infer attempt identity from identical payload bytes: separately authorized attempts may have identical requests. An invocation is identity and custody data, never a self-authorizing token. Reconciliation receives the same original closure, is observational and cannot redispatch it. New mutation admission requires the exact executor to implement its role reconciliation method and currently hold both change and observe access for this scope. Observation remains subject to current authority; earlier admission does not bypass revocation.

SourceTargetBinding.description: Receiving-owner-approved mapping of a host service or software source selector to its exact enrolled executor and canonical native mutation target. The executor role is service or software; its scope and the selected instance must agree, and its change grant must contain the namespace. The owner independently resolves native aliases and verifies the mapping before enrolling it. Source bytes cannot create, replace or authorize this mapping. Different selector spellings or instances that resolve to one namespace remain one target; a host may prescribe that target only once. Native side effects remain confined to the complete accepted mutation grant.

description: Descriptor for a separately approved implementation. Provider-owned configuration, component and source schemas retain their JSON Schema format semantics. Bare date-time asserts RFC3339 syntax and Gregorian calendar validity without normalizing strings or inheriting core Time precision/UTC restrictions. Leap-second syntax is checked only at the offset-adjusted UTC end of a month; actual insertion or negative-leap schedules require provider authority and are not qualification supplied by this validator. Provider schemas assert only date, date-time, ipv4, ipv6 and uuid formats. Unknown formats, nested dialect declarations, dialect vocabularies and unsupported keywords (including unevaluatedItems and unevaluatedProperties) reject during descriptor approval. The profile permits at most 262144 schema bytes, depth 32 and 4096 expanded schema positions. Pattern strings are at most 256 characters, contain no backreferences, lookbehind or inline flags, and variable repetition applies only to character atoms (apart from optional groups), with at most eight alternative paths; only patterns with a linear work bound are admitted. Pattern inputs are at most 4096 characters. Configuration evaluation admits at most 2000000 charged work units including linear regex bounds and compared bytes for const, enum and hash-indexed structural uniqueness; exhausted capacity is an explicit rejection, never successful partial validation. Source configuration bytes retain the separate 1048576-byte boundary.
